Exact primitive: a monotone deque, as used in [Lemire’s streaming extrema algorithm](https://arxiv.org/abs/cs/0610046). The following recurrence is derived for the stated support, assuming fixed pair scores S(i,j), ρ>0, item IDs x_i, and eligibility E(i,j): x_i≠x_j and |i−j|≥3. Without expiration, an existing anchor updates as s[t,i]=max(e^(−1/ρ)s[t−1,i], S(i,t)) when E(i,t); otherwise only decay. Initialize a new anchor with s[t,t]=max_{j≤t−3, x_j≠x_t} S(t,j). Older partners have zero decay at initialization because max(t,j)=t. Empty maxima require an explicit convention: −∞ mathematically; zero only for nonnegative, zero-default support.

For a sliding window [t−W+1,t], the scalar recurrence fails when its winning partner expires. Maintain a separate deque per active anchor, inserting eligible partners chronologically with key K(i,j)=S(i,j)exp(max(i,j)/ρ). Pop dominated tails, expire heads with j<t−W+1, and return exp(−t/ρ) times the head key. Initialize each new anchor by scanning its eligible historical partners; retaining only their maximum loses expiration backups. Drop the anchor’s deque when i expires. Apply masks before insertion; changing scores or eligibility invalidates this construction.

Avoid overflowing exponentials: for positive scores compare log S(i,j)+max(i,j)/ρ, preferably with a rebased time origin; represent zero by −∞. Signed scores require common-scale rebasing rather than logarithms. Each deque operation is amortized O(1) per pair, but all W anchors require O(W) pair processing per event, O(TW) total time, and O(W²) worst-case storage, excluding similarity costs. These are exact real-arithmetic algorithms with ordinary floating-point error; deque speed does not imply constant-cost recommendation updates.
